verdict: Thomson Reuters grew revenue 10% to $1.8B with its 'Big 3' segments each up about 10%, but operating profit fell 22% because a year ago it booked a large one-off gain on selling its Elite stake.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +10% YoY; 88% of it is recurring subscription-style revenue

kpis.label: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.note: +10% YoY, a 35.5% margin — the company's non-IFRS measure

segments.name: Legal Professionals
segments.note: Westlaw, CoCounsel AI and other tools for law firms and legal departments — the biggest segment.

segments.name: Corporates
segments.note: Tax, legal and risk software and content for large companies.

segments.name: Tax, Audit & Accounting Professionals
segments.note: Software and content for tax and accounting firms, including the new CoCounsel Tax, Audit & Accounting.

segments.name: Reuters
segments.note: The Reuters news agency — news sold to media customers and financial professionals.

segments.name: Eliminations and rounding
segments.note: Small amounts eliminated between segments, and rounding.

opex.name: Operating expenses
opex.note: The day-to-day cost of running the business — people, content, technology and offices — as reported under IFRS.

opex.name: Amortization of software
opex.note: Spreading the cost of software the company built or bought over its useful life (a non-cash charge).

opex.name: Depreciation
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings and equipment over their useful lives (a non-cash charge).

opex.name: Amortization of other intangibles
opex.note: Spreading the cost of acquired customer lists, content and other intangible assets (a non-cash charge).

opex.name: Other operating losses
opex.note: A small net other operating loss; a year ago this line was a $160M gain, mostly from selling the remaining stake in Elite.

otherDetail: Net finance costs were $49M ($51M of net interest expense, partly offset by $2M of other finance income), and earnings from discontinued operations added $50M, for net other income of $1M; the share of losses in equity-method investments was a further $5M.

takeaways.title: Broad, subscription-led growth
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 10% to $1,833M, all of it organic (not from deals or currency). Recurring revenue — 88% of the total — grew 9%, and transaction revenue grew 27%. Legal Professionals, Corporates and Tax & Accounting, the 'Big 3', each grew about 10% and together are 88% of revenue.

takeaways.title: Profit fell on a tough comparison
takeaways.text: Operating profit dropped 22% to $402M, mainly because last year's quarter included a $160M gain on selling the remaining minority stake in Elite, and because software amortization rose. Adjusted EBITDA, which strips those out, rose 10% to $651M.

takeaways.title: Net earnings included a business being sold
takeaways.text: Net earnings were $339M, of which $50M came from discontinued operations — Global Print, whose 51% stake was sold to KKR funds for about $500M in gross proceeds on October 1, just after quarter end. Continuing operations earned $289M.

oneTimers: A year ago, other operating gains of $160M — mostly the gain on selling the remaining minority interest in the Elite business — flattered operating profit; this quarter that line was a $1M loss.
Earnings include $50M from discontinued operations (Global Print). The company also issued about $2.0B of new notes in September and finished a $600M share buyback.
footerNote: Thomson Reuters reports under IFRS and does not split out a cost of revenue or gross profit, so revenue flows straight to its reported operating-expense lines. To keep the flow balanced, the $50M of after-tax earnings from discontinued operations (Global Print) is included in other income; earnings from continuing operations were $289M.

sources.label: Official earnings release, Form 6-K Exhibit 99.1 (SEC EDGAR)
